_about: Public, citable courier pricing for COD sellers. Every number here was read off a page that was actually fetched, and carries its source. null means NO public figure was found: Bya3 must ask the seller, never assume. See specs/beginner-pricing.md §3.
_rules: Never invent a value to fill a null. A missing default becomes a question to the seller.
confirmationRatePct and deliveryRatePct have NO public source in any market. They stay null until real seller data (docs/seller-intake.md) provides them.
Bands are [low, high] in the country's own currency, per delivered order, excluding VAT unless noted.
These are list prices. Merchants who negotiate volume rates pay less, and those rates are public nowhere.

EG.notes: Bosta list price by zone, before VAT: Cairo 97, Alexandria 102, Delta/Canal 110, Upper Egypt/Red Sea 140 (small & medium parcels). RTO is a published flat 87 EGP across all four zones — the only courier-stated RTO figure in the region besides Morocco. Treat as a CEILING: the same page says 'higher volume, lower price', and Bosta's own signup flow shows lower numbers (57-82 delivery, 40-65 RTO) that could not be verified without an account. noon's weight-banded 45-79 EGP marketplace fee is the realistic floor. COD collection is included up to 3,000 EGP, then 1% of the excess (terms last modified 2 Jan 2023).

AE.notes: Two published prices that differ by about 2x: Jeebly 17.31 per shipment up to 5 kg next-day, and Quiqup 35 next-day (excluding 5% VAT), +2 AED/kg above 5 kg. No single typical value is defensible. Quiqup is the most useful source found anywhere in the region: it publishes a RULE rather than a number for returns — 'RTO, cancelled orders and failed collections are charged the full delivery fee' — plus a COD fee of 2.5% of the value collected, three delivery attempts in the main emirates and only one in remote areas.

sources.name: Jeebly
sources.date: 2026, blog page not a tariff schedule

MA.notes: The best-evidenced market of the nine. Pickup city 18-28, major cities about 35, outlying regions 40-50. Returns are genuinely free: three COD couriers print a return or refusal column at 0 MAD across hundreds of city rows, and two more state free returns in policy; only OXO prints a non-zero 15 MAD. Caveats: only Chrono Diali publishes a weight band at all, rates change with the departure warehouse, and NO Moroccan page printed any COD commission — the widely repeated '2-5% of COD value' could not be reproduced anywhere.

SA.notes: No courier publishes a national merchant COD rate on its own site: SMSA, Naqel and AyMakan all gate pricing behind calculators, and Aramex blocks retrieval. The only printed named-courier prices come from the Zid platform, excluding tax, for a first 10 kg band: SPL 20, Aramex 23, SMSA 23. Salla's 'from 13 SAR' is a marketing floor with no weight band. Zid states returns cost no extra beyond the basic shipping price, but the wording is ambiguous and no amount is given.

sources.name: SPL / Saudi Post
sources.for: bundle pricing (conflicts with its own catalogue)

BH.notes: No merchant COD rate published. Bahrain Post's counter tariff (1.200 BHD up to 2 kg, rising to 8.400 at 20 kg) is a retail rate, not a courier rate for sellers, and Bahrain Post has no COD product. The regulator sets a price floor for licensed couriers but publishes no rates.

KW.notes: Nothing published. Couriers price by distance or vertical inside their own apps.

QA.notes: Qatar Post routes every service to a calculator; no per-order rate is printed.

OM.notes: Asyad Express's pricing page contains no figures and its calculator reports the service unavailable.

JO.notes: Nothing found for any courier: the large ones block automated retrieval and are calculators regardless, and local firms are quote-form only.

DZ.notes: Not researched yet. Algeria has large COD courier networks (Yalidine, ZR Express) that may publish rates.
